missat: UG_3_H1 contradicts itself: "a parent speaks in her own words, no script read aloud" — and then a word-for-word Swedish script with "Swedish captions word for word". The editor cannot produce both.

GT_4_H1 opens on the verbatim quote `Bra adventskalender. Rolig idé …` — a fine quote, a weak first second: nothing to see, and "bra adventskalender" is a line any calendar could carry. Open on the child's hand at door 1 and place the quote at 3–6 s.
Hypotheses without numbers: "the gift angle is the one profitable active ad" (GT_4_H1), "the first UGC parent is the strongest new signal" (UG_3_H1) — cite CPA and purchases against break-even.
The code BF holds three different angles this round (count, rating, rolling wheels: BF_10/11/12) — the next /cs cannot group by angle. Rating belongs in RV/SP, the wheels in PD.
No Variables line on any brief; 5 of 9 concepts have no source named; no COPY CARD. The three-question table is ✅✅❌ on every line.
This product has no memory in the repo linked to the hub (products/kalender/ is the closed OPS store's) — the Feedback row in the hub is its memory.
regler: A brief is either scripted or UGC: for UGC write the beats and the facts the parent must get right, mark the captions "summarize her words", and never write "word for word".
One concept code = one angle: keep BF for one thing, put ratings in RV, the rolling wheels in PD — and add the Variables line to every brief.
Cite the parent's CPA and purchases against break-even in every Why that calls something a winner — "the one profitable ad" and "the strongest new signal" need numbers.

fel: The brief contradicts itself: "a parent speaks to camera in her own words, no script read aloud" versus a word-for-word Swedish script and "Swedish captions word for word". Decide before shooting: either a scripted VO (then it is not UGC) or a real parent in her own words with captions that summarize what she says. The facts she must get right: 24 doors, 24 different cars, wheels that roll, 499 kr / 649 kr, från 3 år.
